skill.name: paypal-integration
skill.description: Integrate PayPal payment processing with support for express checkout, subscriptions, and refund management. Use when implementing PayPal payments, processing online transactions, or building e-commerce checkout flows.
skill.summary: Guide PayPal checkout, subscriptions, IPN processing, refunds, and sandbox testing.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Static command detections are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and inline resource paths. The network findings are expected PayPal and local callback examples, with no evidence of exfiltration or prompt injection. Two high-severity semantic issues were added for payment flows that omit server-side amount, merchant, and IPN business validation.

remediation.issue: Client-side checkout defines the payment amount in browser code.
remediation.suggestion: Create orders on the server from trusted cart data, then verify amount, currency, merchant, status, and capture ID before fulfillment.

remediation.issue: IPN handling verifies PayPal authenticity but omits business validation before fulfillment.
remediation.suggestion: After VERIFIED, compare receiver, amount, currency, invoice, and order identifiers against trusted records before updating orders.

remediation.issue: Network examples omit timeouts and response status checks.
remediation.suggestion: Add request timeouts, handle non-success responses, and validate PayPal response fields before using returned data.

semantic_findings.title: Client-Side Payment Amount Can Be Tampered
semantic_findings.description: The quick-start creates the order amount in browser code and captures using only the submitted order ID. A copied implementation could allow users to change amount or currency before capture because server-side validation is not shown.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited flow places the value in client code and returns captured amount without comparing it to a trusted order record. PayPal integrations can be safe if the author adds validation, so confidence is high but not absolute.

semantic_findings.title: Incomplete IPN Business Validation
semantic_findings.description: The IPN example verifies the message with PayPal, then processes completed payments without checking receiver identity, expected amount, currency, or order mapping. A copied implementation could fulfill goods for a mismatched payment notification.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code gates on PayPal VERIFIED and payment_status, then reaches fulfillment comments. It is illustrative documentation, so confidence is high but not absolute.

content.user_title: Build PayPal Checkout and Billing Flows
content.value_statement: Payment integrations can fail when checkout, subscriptions, refunds, and webhooks are handled separately. This skill gives practical PayPal patterns for building and reviewing those flows.
actual_capabilities: Guides PayPal Checkout with Smart Buttons and REST order capture.
Shows a Python PayPal client for OAuth tokens, order creation, capture, and order details.
Explains IPN verification and payment state handling.
Provides subscription plan and subscriber setup examples.
Covers refund creation and refund lookup patterns.
Lists sandbox testing steps and common implementation pitfalls.
limitations: Examples require adaptation before production use.
Does not manage compliance, tax, fraud, or chargeback policy decisions.
Does not provide live credentials or create PayPal developer accounts.
Some snippets omit full database, authentication, and deployment controls.

use_cases.title: Add Store Checkout
use_cases.description: Plan a PayPal one-time payment flow for products, carts, and server-side capture.

use_cases.title: Launch Subscription Billing
use_cases.description: Design recurring PayPal plans, subscriber approval links, and renewal handling.

use_cases.title: Operate Refunds And Disputes
use_cases.description: Map refund requests, chargeback events, and transaction lookup steps.

prompt_templates.title: Start Checkout
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement PayPal Checkout for a small store that sells fixed-price products. Include server-created orders, capture validation, and sandbox testing steps.

prompt_templates.title: Handle IPN Events
prompt_templates.prompt: Design PayPal IPN handling for completed payments, refunds, and chargebacks. Include verification, duplicate prevention, and order update rules.

prompt_templates.title: Create Subscriptions
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a PayPal subscription flow for monthly plans. Include plan creation, approval routing, renewal tracking, and cancellation handling.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my PayPal integration design before launch. Check server validation, credential handling, error handling, retries, logging, and sandbox coverage.

output_examples.input: A developer asks for one-time PayPal checkout for a cart.
output: A checkout flow with server-created orders and client approval.
A validation checklist for amount, currency, status, merchant, and duplicate capture.
Sandbox test cases for successful payment, cancellation, and failed capture.

output_examples.input: A SaaS team asks for recurring billing guidance.
output: A subscription plan workflow with product, plan, subscriber, and approval steps.
Event handling notes for renewals, failed payments, cancellations, and refunds.
Operational checks for plan identifiers, customer records, and billing status.

output_examples.input: A support team asks how to process refunds.
output: A refund workflow for full and partial refunds.
A transaction lookup process for support review.
A dispute response checklist with logging and customer notification steps.

best_practices: Create and capture orders from trusted server data, then verify amount, currency, merchant, and status.
Use PayPal sandbox and test buyer and seller accounts before using live credentials.
Handle duplicate notifications, refunds, reversals, and network failures idempotently.
anti_patterns: Do not trust browser callbacks as proof of payment.
Do not hardcode live credentials or environment URLs in application source.
Do not fulfill orders before server-side PayPal verification completes.

faq.question: Does this skill create a complete PayPal application?
faq.answer: No. It provides integration patterns and examples that must be adapted to your application.

faq.question: Does it cover PayPal Checkout?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Smart Buttons, order creation, order capture, and order detail lookup patterns.

faq.question: Does it support subscriptions?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for subscription plans, subscriber creation, and approval links.

faq.question: Does it handle refunds?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes refund creation and refund detail lookup guidance.

faq.question: Can I use the examples in production without changes?
faq.answer: No. Add server-side validation, secure credential storage, authentication, logging controls, and complete error handling.
